notes: All five styles transcribed from the Richmond page itself; no rule imported from any Rheem-family file and no usesStylesOf set, even though some shapes resemble Rheem-family serials. The page states Richmond is a Paloma brand and that the serials shown are utilized with all Paloma brand systems. Factory-letter styles (2 and 4) are encoded with absolute positions as the schema requires, with the factory letter fixed at the index shown in each page example and week/year as the first four digits after it. Style 3 counting: character counting is confirmed and digit-only counting falsified (digit-only 2nd-3rd digits would give week 91, invalid; character positions give week 29, year 2010).

styles.era: Month-year serials: 4 digits, 1 letter, then digits
styles.notes: Page states month is 1st and 2nd numerical digits and year is 3rd and 4th numerical digits.

Page states the date is coded in the middle group following a letter designation of F or M, representing week and year; in the example the letter M sits at index 5, so week is positions [6,8] and year [8,10].
Page states week is 2nd and 3rd numerical digits and year is 4th and 5th numerical digits, counted as character positions: digit-only counting is falsified (it would give week 91).

Page states the date is coded in the middle group following a letter designation of F or M, representing week and year; in the example the letter F sits at index 7, so week is positions [8,10] and year [10,12].

styles.era: 9-digit serials, date in last four digits
styles.notes: Page states the date is coded in the last four digits of the 9-digit serial, representing week and year.
